taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-20, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 64.6 | 2.65 | 2.65
2 | 775.4 | 0.67 | 3.32
3 | 110.3 | 1.09 | 4.41
4 | 222.5 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-20, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-20, located in survey area T, consists of four interpreted layers with resistivity values of 64.6 $\Omega$m, 775.4 $\Omega$m, 110.3 $\Omega$m, and 222.5 $\Omega$m. Following the curve-type notation rules, the first triplet (64.6, 775.4, 110.3) follows the K pattern ($r_1 < r_2 > r_3$), and the second triplet (775.4, 110.3, 222.5) follows the H pattern ($r_1 > r_2 < r_3$). Consequently, the correct curve type is KH. Please note that the A-type classification currently on file is incorrect and does not match the interpreted layer resistivities.

{"curve_type_stated": "KH", "label_issue_flagged": true}
